knowledge_gaps: The recency residual is a reasonable first experiment, but its advantage over last-item and order-insensitive pooling is untested. Originality 4/10 is plausible; potential 7/10 is speculative, and difficulty 3/10 understates the diagnostic work.

Implementation omits embedding scaling, dropout placement, residual normalization relative to SASRec, initialization order, and gate-gradient monitoring. These choices affect baseline comparability and whether the near-zero gate learns.

Replay construction is underspecified: prefix selection, user counts, deletion sizes, random-control overlap with recent deletions, candidate generation, repeated-target eligibility, and tie handling need explicit rules. Training-prefix performance also reflects fitted examples.

Position-based decay measures interaction recency rather than elapsed time. Neither recency pooling nor the proposed probes directly tests repeated semantic interests, compatibility, or immediate usefulness.
The experiment lacks a concrete GPU budget, checkpoint-selection protocol, uncertainty reporting, and numerical verification that training and generated predictors produce matching scores.
